questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Well reputed private institution good to have on the CV.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Duke was extremely service-oriented and provided everything I needed in timely manner.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Practical information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Get at least a bike or preferably a car to get around. Distances are great, although Uber is easy and relatively affordable. Some places feel a little unsafe outside of campus at night.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All housing very near to campus is extremely expensive, consider taking something a little further away for half the price and get some space and air.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Everything is through DukeHub and manuals are sent in advance as well as an online prep meeting with guidance on which courses to chose and avoid. It was possible to change courses the first two weeks of classes as long as there was open spots, so one could try out different things.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Dean of International Studies was very helpful and the system was intuitive.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful as long as you are ready for when the course registration opens.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the course catalogue thoroughly and discuss your thoughts with the Dean.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very different depending on the course.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Lower level courses does not mean less coursework but maybe even more "grunt" or basic work as it is mandatory courses for the US first year students. Higher level courses are more high level and general but with a precondition of some general knowledge on the US law system but very doable with some independent research in advance.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Professors teach their courses themselves and use the socratic method, so be prepared to be asked in front of the entire class involuntarily ("cold-called") but it is less intimidating than it sounds as long as one has read the material.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Business Associations
- Negotiation for Lawyers
- Financial Valuation
- Structuring and Regulating Financial Transactions

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
- Business Associations is a must for everyone going to the US to understand the common law thinking in civil procedure for corporations.
- Negotiation for Lawyers was the break of the week and a nice practical hands-on course, probably my favourite.
- Financial Valuation is good for everyone interested in finance and investment banking, you are thrown into deep water but helped and it is fun.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Groceries are super expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Books, most were freely available from the school if you did not want to buy them, otherwise they were expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Amazing facilities at campus, lots of activities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything imaginable, especially sporting events, fitness together, "bar review" every Thursday, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take use of the Wilson Recreational Center and enjoy doing sports for free everyday.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Roadtrips! Hiking is good around the area also. The international community is great and there is always someone hosting something.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes, Americans are very easy to engage and I felt very included from day 1.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to them before and after class, very easy to interact and they are curious to see new faces.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Avoiding fastfood.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: College sports and events.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Grades are normal distributed and the JD students are very good and competitive, so it is almost impossible coming from outside and get better grades than average. Typically, the LLM students get less than average because the natives have an advantage.
2) Enjoy being free from all obligations encountered in Copenhagen, no study job and relational maintenance, but pure pleasure and freedom.
3) Get a car so you can easily get around and go on weekend trips, there is never class on Fridays, so a three-day weekend is easy to spend away.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Duke Law School is fantastic, try it and enjoy - it is pretty chill after all.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Networking with very talented and ambitious students, now I know someone in all major US and EU cities.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first two weeks of new impressions, vocabulary and US law traditions.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
